s: HTTP-accessible blob store providing virtually unlimited durable storage for files, backups, and static assets at low cost.
w: Objects (files + metadata) are stored in buckets with flat key namespaces; access is via REST API (GET/PUT/DELETE). Data is replicated across availability zones automatically; versioning preserves object history. Lifecycle policies transition objects between tiers (standard, infrequent, glacier) based on age. Pre-signed URLs grant temporary access without exposing credentials. Event notifications trigger functions or queues on upload/delete.
use: Media storage: user uploads, images, videos, audio files
Backup and disaster recovery destinations for database snapshots
Static website hosting and SPA bundle storage
Data lake foundation for analytics pipelines (Parquet/Avro files)
CDN origin for cached content delivery
avoid: Frequent small reads requiring low latency (use block_storage or database instead)
Structured data requiring SQL queries (use a database)
Real-time mutable files (object storage is optimized for write-once/read-many)

size.objects_per_bucket: Unlimited; throughput scales with prefix parallelism

pat.d: Object storage serves as origin; CDN caches at edge for low-latency delivery.

pits: High request costs from millions of small object reads - batch or cache in front of object storage
Lifecycle policy misconfiguration deleting production data - test policies on non-critical buckets first
tips: Object storage IS the foundation of cloud: S3-like services underpin backups, data lakes, CDNs, and ML training data
Pre-signed URLs eliminate the need for a proxy server for temporary file access
